propositions: Repository-wide documentation and comment surfaces must conform to formal voice, complete sentences, no contractions, precise verbs, prohibited punctuation rules, and eliminated filler across three shard categories: durable records plus internal documentation, external documentation plus shipped help, and developer comments plus embedded prose.

Maintained authored prose must exclude em dashes, en dashes, spaced hyphens, semicolons, and clause-connecting colons; hyphens limited to compound words and technical names; every Markdown paragraph on one logical line; adjectives used only when selecting from multiple options; and filler terms deleted.

Documentation ownership, lifecycle, canonical sources, citation rules, generated artifact rules, and historical correction procedures must be formalized in a policy document establishing audience matrices, external versus internal distinctions, and governance for tickets, ADRs, and internal documentation.

Prose validation must be integrated with make targets and portable CI paths, covering Markdown, help text, package metadata, YAML, TOML, HCL, shell text, workflow annotations, and schema descriptions, with manual review for structural elements and formal voice.

Generated documentation artifacts require explicit ownership registration linking canonical sources, derived outputs, drift checks, and regeneration contracts for configuration reference, ADR index, CLI reference, and MCP reference.
Comment hygiene must expand beyond selected Python trees to validate that comments provide developer context without repeating code, reiterating historical narration, or serving as conversations.
